books.title: Duck, Sir Hopsalot!
books.blurb: Sir Hopsalot, the most boastful bunny in the park, pushes in at the Rail Race and challenges RiPika, then bonks every striped bar because he thinks ‘duck’ means a duck, until RiPika slows down to teach him, wins anyway, and wins a friend.
books.adversary: Sir Hopsalot, a pompous white bunny (the bunny model) with the tallest ears in the park: a rival and a real show-off. He pushes in at the Rail Race queue, calls RiPika ‘small yellow person’ and challenges her to a race, then bonks bar after bar because nobody ever told him that ‘duck’ means get down low. Resolved by sportsmanship, not by a secret sorrow: RiPika could win easily but slows down to teach him; they duck the last bar side by side; she still wins, by the tip of her nose; he keeps his promise to call her magnificent (and they argue happily about which of them is more magnificent); and the next day he says sorry for pushing in, gives her a rubber duck and hops to the back of the queue. A rival beaten fair and square and won over. He is not misunderstood: he really was rude, and he changes.
jokes: p1: the boasting: tallest ears, fluffiest tail, never stops telling everybody about it, and ‘He even told the trees.’
p3: caught pushing in, he sniffs ‘Nonsense’ and challenges the ‘small yellow person’ to a race
p4: ‘DUCK!’ / ‘A duck? Where?’ / BONK! His ears go wibble-wobble (the running gag starts)
p5: He peered left. He peered right. He peered up. BONK! ‘Still no duck,’ he grumbled.
p6: ‘Everybody keeps shouting about ducks, and there are no ducks anywhere!’
p9: an argument made entirely of compliments, ‘You are magnificent.’ ‘So are you!’ ‘No, YOU are!’, all the way to the ice cream parlour
p10: the payoff, a rubber duck: ‘At last,’ laughed RiPika, ‘a duck!’
throughout: his name (Sir Hopsalot hops a lot)

books.title: Detective Biscuit
books.blurb: When a balloon, a keyring and a breakfast bowl vanish, Detective Biscuit follows pancake-shaped footprints, sets a trap and catches a naughty-looking mini, who turns out to have been keeping everyone’s lost things safe.
books.adversary: A mini (createMini: the ‘MINI ATTACK!’ creature from Mayhem mode), a tiny lilac creature with grabby arms and eyebrows that look naughty even when it is asleep. RiPika’s balloon comes untied, your keyring falls off your bag and Biscuit forgets his bowl by the pink wall; all three vanish and its pancake footprints turn up everywhere, so Biscuit baits a trap with a gold star and catches it. The one adversary on the shelf who is purely misunderstood, and the trap turns round on the detective: it didn’t take the star, it found it. It never stole anything. It found what people lost and kept it safe behind the pink wall, and could never give anything back, because whenever it ran up shouting ‘MINI ATTACK!’ everybody took one look at its eyebrows and ran. Biscuit lets it keep the star as its Finder of Lost Things badge, and a mini attack turns out to be a knee-high hug.
jokes: p3: ‘Our thief,’ he said, ‘has very funny feet.’
p4: Biscuit’s three clues (small, funny feet, loves breakfast) describe Biscuit himself. ‘My feet aren’t funny!’ Everyone looks at his feet. They were, a bit.
p5: hiding behind the fountain, Biscuit’s tummy rumbles: ‘I can’t shush a tummy!’
p7: the trap turns round: the mini didn’t TAKE the star, it FOUND it, lying on the path all alone, and Biscuit, who left it there, has to admit that is perfectly true
p9: its eyebrows look naughty even when it is asleep
p10: a mini attack is really a hug, a very small one, round your knees

books.title: The Loudest Shush
books.blurb: Trilla the singing puff cannot stop singing in the library, and grumpy Mrs Crumpet, the library cat left in charge, shushes louder every time, until Trilla spots a yawn and finds a clever, kind way round the rule.
books.adversary: Mrs Crumpet, the grumpy ginger library cat (the kitten model, always on her pile of books), left in charge while the owl librarian is out. A grump whose every SHHHH is louder than the singing, humming or hiccupping it is meant to stop. Outwitted kindly, not misunderstood: when her biggest shush comes out as a yawn, Trilla works out that this grumpy cat is a sleepy cat, and finds a loophole: ‘I’m not singing, I’m lullabying.’ Mrs Crumpet can find no rule against that, and every shush she tries turns into another yawn until she is fast asleep, purring like a tractor, and the shusher gets shushed. Nothing about her turns out secretly sweet; she simply gets the naps she needed, Trilla gets to sing, and Trilla lullabies her to sleep every nap time after.
jokes: p1: she even sings in her sleep, ‘which is very tricky indeed’ (the picture: notes and zzzs floating up together)
p3: Mrs Crumpet is in charge and takes it very seriously, with her eyes shut
p4: her SHHHHHH is so loud that every page flutters: the shush is always louder than the noise (the running gag)
p5: the shush wobbles a lamp and makes a mouse drop his book; ‘I can hear you THINKING about humming.’
p6: Trilla holds her song in until she puffs up round, rounder, the roundest puff there is, then hiccups out notes: ‘HIC!’
p7: her biggest shush yet comes out as an enormous YAWN
p8: the loophole: ‘I’m not singing, I’m lullabying. It’s much quieter.’ She could not find a rule against that.
p9: every shush she tries turns into a yawn
p10: she purrs like a tractor and the bookshelves rattle, so Trilla shushes the shusher: ‘Shhh, Mrs Crumpet!’

books.title: The Giant Footprints
books.blurb: Giant footprints appear all over the park and everyone hides, until brave RiPika works out that whoever made them walks far too slowly to be scary and follows them to Grandpa Tock, a 102-year-old tortoise who has never been on a ride.
books.adversary: ‘The giant’: dinner-plate footprints circle the fountain, nibble every yellow flower and creep towards the rides, until Sir Hopsalot, the mouse and Biscuit are all hiding. There is no villain, only a scary rumour, and it is beaten by courage and a clear head: brave RiPika sees that the prints are very close together, so whoever made them walks very slowly, and nothing that slow can be scary. She follows the trail to Grandpa Tock, the 102-year-old tortoise in the Reptile House’s Tortoise Garden, who sets off for the Rail Race every evening but is so slow that the carts are asleep when he arrives. The ending is a kindness rather than a confession: RiPika calls the cat bus to carry him, everyone who hid from him comes out to wave, and after a hundred and two years he gets his ride.
jokes: p2: RiPika’s foot in a giant footprint looks like a pea on a dinner plate; ‘And probably a very big tummy.’
p3: ‘It likes yellow things,’ says RiPika, who is very yellow, and she hides behind you, just in case
p4: ‘A GIANT HAMSTER!’ wails Biscuit, from under a bench
p7: Grandpa Tock wakes up so slowly that it takes him until lunchtime to say good morning
p10: he doesn’t need to duck on the Rail Race, he just pops his head into his shell; and at the finish, ‘Again! But slower, please.’

books.title: Biscuit and the Storm
books.blurb: When a scowling storm cloud rains on the Grand Fountain Picnic, Biscuit’s own tummy tells him why it is so cross, so he and RiPika brave the wind to feed it, and the greedy bear ends up sharing his picnic with a new friend called Nimbus.
books.adversary: A huge grey storm cloud (a book-only stormCloud model) that scowls, rumbles and rains on the Grand Fountain Picnic, and whose wind blows the sandwiches away. It really is cross, and for a reason Biscuit knows better than anyone: when its rumble comes again and his own tummy rumbles back, he realises that it is not thunder at all but a hungry tummy. Won over by kindness and sharing rather than by a misunderstanding cleared up: Biscuit and RiPika march out into the storm for candy floss and carry it up the lift to the castle roof; the cloud gobbles it, burps a rainbow, blows every sandwich back and says its name is Nimbus; and the greedy bear who packed forty-two sandwiches as ‘a little snack’ gives it forty-one of them. Here the hero is the one who changes.

p10: Nimbus gets forty-one sandwiches and Biscuit gets one, and the book ends: ‘And whose tummy rumbled all the way home?’

books.title: Catch That Chicken!
books.blurb: An hour before the Space Ferris Wheel climbs to space, Chicken-looter pinches its golden star, and you and Trilla chase him across the evening sky by jet pack, then win the star back with a better offer.
books.adversary: Chicken-looter, the cheeky white-and-red chicken balloon (balloon, variant chicken) who loves shiny things, pinches the Space Ferris Wheel’s golden star an hour before its eight o’clock climb. A real trickster, and still a cheeky one at the end. He is outwitted twice, kindly: Trilla spots his feathery bottom poking out of the cloud he hides in; and when, sitting on the star in his nest of pinched treasures, he admits that shiny things are his night-lights because he is scared of the dark, you offer him a better deal: ‘The dark isn’t scary. It’s where the stars live. Give back one star, and you can see millions!’ He hands back the star and the disco ball (never the biscuit), you click the star in a minute before eight, and he rides to space, not scared one bit and so happy that he lays a surprise egg.

p7: scared or not, he sits on the star, just in case, like a hen on an egg
p8: he gives back the star. And the disco ball. But not the biscuit.
p10: he is so happy that he lays an egg. ‘A surprise egg, of course!’

notes:
EDITOR’S NOTES, 16 Oct 2026. Every edit the judge asked for is made and every page is recounted; what follows is what changed, why, and what the shelf still needs.

SHELF ORDER (kept as the judge set it): 1 Duck, Sir Hopsalot! 2 Detective Biscuit 3 The Loudest Shush 4 The Giant Footprints 5 Biscuit and the Storm 6 Catch That Chicken! I tried every other order of the middle four against the shelf’s hard rules. The rules: Hopsalot first, as the step up from Duck, Duck, Duck! and so that Sir Hopsalot is met before his cameos; Shush before Storm, so Mrs Crumpet is introduced before she sleeps through the storm; the two footprint mysteries apart; the two Biscuit books apart; the bedtime book last. Only this order passes all of them. Its one cost is that Detective p5’s one-line shush joke stands next to The Loudest Shush. I kept it, because ‘I can’t shush a tummy!’ is a different joke from a whole book of shushing.

HOW THE SIX NOW RESOLVE (the judge’s note that every adversary turned out to be misunderstood). Only one is purely misunderstood now; each of the other five ends a different way.
1 Sir Hopsalot: a rival beaten fair and square and won over. He really was rude, and on p10 (new) he says sorry for pushing in and queues at the back.
2 The mini: misunderstood. This is the classic mystery twist, with Biscuit’s trap kept and turned back on the detective.
3 Mrs Crumpet: outwitted kindly. Her sad confession on p8 is cut. Trilla spots the yawn (p7) and finds a loophole, ‘I’m not singing, I’m lullabying’ (p8). Every shush then turns into a yawn (p9), and the shusher gets shushed (p10). Nothing about her turns out secretly sweet.
4 The giant: no villain at all, only a rumour, beaten by courage and deduction and ended with a kindness: Grandpa Tock’s first ride.
5 The storm: a cloud that really is cross, because it is hungry. ‘That’s not thunder. That’s a hungry TUMMY! No wonder that cloud is cross’ replaces ‘That cloud isn’t cross’. It is won over by a gift and by sharing, and here it is the hero who changes: forty-one sandwiches to one.
6 Chicken-looter: a trickster outwitted twice, kindly. Trilla spots the feathery bottom (kept). Then comes a clever trade, ‘Give back one star, and you can see millions!’ (p8), which keeps the bedtime line. ‘Suddenly he didn’t seem cheeky at all’ is replaced by ‘Then he sat on the star, just in case’ (p7). He stays cheeky, keeps the biscuit, and the sitting sets up the egg.

THE JUDGE’S EDITS, AS MADE.
- Hopsalot: the optional p1 line, ‘He even told the trees.’ Every cart a pet rides is at size 0.4, with the rider at SEAT_HEIGHT 0.958. Ducking riders are sunk into the tub. The p4 and p5 bars are brought down until they meet his ear tips. The biggest bar is left unscaled and set nearer the camera. On p8 he is sunk low, ear tips just under the bar.
- Detective: the things are genuinely lost (p1 is the judge’s wording). It says keyring and ice cream parlour. The ‘MINI ATTACK!’ shout is the mini’s own (p9). The specs name createMini, a grab amount on the actor, createPinkWall({ length: 2 }), and a no-keyring kid on p1.
- Shush: ‘Out of Trilla popped a song, all by itself’ (p4). ‘Round, then rounder, then the roundest puff there is’, drawn at size 1.3 (p6). A mouse dropped his book (p5). The kitten is Mrs Crumpet on every page.
- Footprints: the mouse replaces the kitten on p4 and p9. Sir Hopsalot’s cameo is explicit on p4, with the verbs swapped so that it is the mouse who squeaks. p9 is split into two sentences. The tortoise needs its head and face exposed, a blink mood and a head-in pose. On p10 the cart is at size 0.4 and Tock at about 0.7.
- Storm: the cloud is a book-only stormCloud model. The owl is createLibraryOwl, with mood surprised for her shush face. Mrs Crumpet is drawn exactly as in Shush and named on p4. There is no kitten at the picnic. The floss is createCandyFloss pink, blue and rainbow.
- Catch: the wheel is a primitive stand-in, not createFerrisWheelProp. Jet packs are mounted the way WornJetpack.ts does it, with createJetpack(0.6) for Trilla. The alien saucer gets setPresence(1) and stands small and far back. No gondola.

MY OTHER CHANGES, WITH REASONS.
- Detective p2: Biscuit puts his bowl down by the pink wall and forgets it, where the judge had it left on a wall. The 0.72 m mini could not reach the top of the 1.3 m wall, and its whole defence is that nobody looks down. The change also plants the pink wall as a fair clue before the mini comes out from behind it.
- Footprints: p1’s 23-word sentence is split. On p5, ‘looked closely: … very close together’ becomes ‘looked carefully’.
- Hopsalot pictures: the finish line is the Rail Race’s real six-band rainbow arch (track.ts), not a chequered banner.
- Storm p8: the castle roof is drawn as its real roof garden with a battlement in buildingWall. The Storm library pages share one dim lighting.
- Pets (bunny, kitten, mouse and Trilla) are built with limbs: null, so no page asks them for a pose. Poses are only on the kid, RiPika, Biscuit and the mini.
- The house face has no yawn and no burp. Mrs Crumpet’s yawn and Nimbus’s burp both use surprised (wide eyes and an ‘oh’ mouth), and the specs say so.

HOUSE STYLE: dialogue in curly singles, curly doubles inside them (Detective p9), curly apostrophes and the single ellipsis character. A script checked that the file has no straight quote anywhere. British names: keyring, ice cream parlour, candy floss, queue, grey, cosy.

COUNTS: a word is a whitespace-separated token containing a letter or a digit, so a hyphenated word counts once. All 60 pages are 28 to 35 words (mean 32.2), and all six books have 10 pages. The longest sentence on the shelf is 20 words; the sentence splitter was first proved against a planted 25-word control. Titles run 17 to 21 characters. Ids are camelCase and unique, and none is one of the twelve picture books’ ids.

CANON FOR THE SHELF:
- Sir Hopsalot is the bunny model, a he. He has cameos in Shush p2, Footprints p4 and p9, and Storm p10.
- Mrs Crumpet is the kitten on her pile of books, and the kitten model is used for nothing else.
- Nimbus is the storm cloud.
- The owl is a she, and her only faces are neutral, blink, happy and shush.
- Chicken-looter appears only in Catch, and the mini only in Detective.

STILL TO BUILD (the judge’s list, not done here):
- A chapter-book tier in check:brevity and check:book-reader (8 to 10 pages, 24 to 36 words a page), with Jim’s 14 October exception written into the BREVITY RULE.
- A reader page layout for about 30 words at the TEXT RULE minimum.
- Six more readable shelf slots, and a decision on whether the prize stays at all twelve or becomes all eighteen.
- New picture models from existing factories, each with a pictureWarmSteps entry: mini, pinkWall, tortoise, owl, candyFloss, jetpack, discoBall, lollipopTree, surpriseEgg and alienSaucer, plus the book-only stormCloud.
- Picture-schema fields: a no-keyring kid, a mini grab amount, a tortoise blink and head-in pose, and a worn jet pack.
- Story licence to know about: the wheel’s golden star and its eight o’clock climb are invented, so a child may go looking for the star.

Nothing in the repository was edited; this JSON is the only file written.
